title: Cloudflare Open Sources Decision Models for AI Agents
gist: Cloudflare open-sourced Clef, 27B and 9B (Clef-Flash) multimodal decision models that return typed answer probabilities in a single forward pass rather than generating text, positioning them as the fast decision layer for AI agents. It competes with Typesafe AI's Jev System One model, and community reaction questions novelty and benchmark credibility.

insights.claim: Cloudflare released Clef, a 27B multimodal open-weight model that takes a state and a schema of typed questions and returns a probability for each allowed option in a single forward pass, with no free-form text generation or output parsing.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Decision models turn agent routing into a cheap classification call instead of an LLM generation.

insights.claim: Clef-Flash is a 9B multimodal model for latency-sensitive decisions, with median latency of 38.8 ms versus 209.3 ms for the 27B Clef in Cloudflare's benchmarks.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: A roughly 5x latency gap lets builders trade accuracy for speed in the agent hot path.

insights.claim: Cloudflare says its edge GPUs give low network latency so Clef can sit in the agent hot path and be combined with an LLM on Workers AI to take action.
insights.speaker: Michelle Chen, Alex Reneau and Kevin Flansburg (Cloudflare)
insights.so_what: Edge inference is Cloudflare's differentiator for agent infrastructure.
insights.quote: Because they are hosted on Cloudflare’s infrastructure, we’re able to take advantage of our GPUs at the edge, leading to low network latency and faster decisions.
insights.locator: Because they are hosted on Cloudflare’s infrastructure

insights.claim: Clef is available through Workers AI and as downloadable weights on Hugging Face, and Cloudflare announced a fine-tuning service, initially with Cloudflare engineers' help and a self-service platform later with no firm date.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Fine-tuning on customers' labelled data is the likely monetization path.
insights.locator: Cloudflare also announced a fine-tuning service

insights.claim: Cloudflare plans to fine-tune Clef for use cases such as support triage and bot classification using its historical labelled data.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Signals first-party applications in support and bot management.

insights.claim: Cloudflare's API is compatible with Typesafe AI's Jev System One model, and Clef differs by adding a vision encoder for images (Jev does text only) and a 64k context window versus Jev's 32k.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Cloudflare is positioning as a drop-in, multimodal alternative to an incumbent decision model.
insights.locator: First, it has a vision encoder

insights.claim: A decision model classifies inputs into typed outcomes with probabilities so agents can decide to act, such as routing, escalating or deferring a support request to a human.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Defines the category role: a probabilistic gate in agent workflows.

insights.claim: A Hacker News commenter argued decision models are not a new paradigm but low-hanging fruit that Typesafe was first to pick up and market heavily.
insights.speaker: Jacek Złydach
insights.so_what: Category novelty may be overstated, so differentiation will rest on execution and distribution.
insights.locator: On a popular Hacker News thread

insights.claim: A commenter warned that public benchmarks are easy to cheat, suggesting a vendor could release a public benchmark to steer attention toward overfitting.
insights.speaker: SebastianSosa
insights.so_what: Treat vendor-linked benchmark results with caution.
insights.locator: The benchmark results raised further questions

insights.claim: A Reddit commenter said what matters is whether Clef knows when to punt, advising tests where false positives cost far more than misses and where data shift reveals when confidence collapses.
insights.speaker: bugra_sa
insights.so_what: Calibration under asymmetric costs is the real production test for decision models.
